what: The heuristic identifies depot/customer location and visited facts from grounded fact names, then reconstructs a complete directed routing-cost matrix once in new() from the metric costs of grounded visit and return-to-depot operators. It optionally retrieves load, capacity, and per-customer demands only by exact numeric names; if translation removed capacity or demand fluents, the resource model is disabled without affecting routing. For each state it finds the current location and unvisited customers, constructs a nearest-neighbor completion that returns to the depot whenever the known residual capacity is insufficient, and computes an MST over the depot, current endpoint, and unvisited customers. The returned estimate is 80% greedy completion cost plus 20% MST cost.
why: CVRP states encode a partial route with a single current endpoint, monotonic customer visits, optional capacity-forced depot transitions, and a mandatory final depot return. A constructive completion therefore gives substantially stronger guidance than merely counting goals or using a pure spanning-tree bound. The representative instances also exhibit strong spatial clusters and expensive inter-cluster arcs, which nearest-neighbor routing and the global MST structure both capture. Blending the two retains decisive route guidance while reducing nearest-neighbor myopia. Grounded operator costs are used because they remain reliable when the translator folds or removes travel-cost, capacity, and demand numeric variables.
